c.tagline: Volcanic peaks, hidden bays, and the gateway to the Grenadines.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are set by route/zone rather than metered; agree the price before departing, especially from the airport or ferry terminal.

emergency.note: Milton Cato Memorial Hospital in Kingstown is the main referral hospital

avoid.reason: Keep usual watch for petty theft around the market and quiet streets after dark.

hood_desc: Compact downtown of Kingstown with the market, cathedrals, waterfront and ferry terminal to the Grenadines; suits budget travelers, business visitors and those wanting to be near shops and transport links.
The most popular beach strip on the island, with a string of small resorts facing Young Island and calm swimming water; suits leisure travelers wanting sand, snorkeling and easy restaurant access.

A quieter residential/marina area next to the yachting hub at Blue Lagoon, popular with sailors and those wanting a low-key base near dive shops and the Botanic Gardens; suits independent travelers with a rental car.

Inland area near the old E.T. Joshua airfield and sports grounds, with guesthouses and easy access to Kingstown and the airport highway; suits budget travelers and those in town for business or cricket matches.
A yachtie-favorite Grenadine island a short ferry ride from Kingstown, with a laid-back harbor town, beaches and a strong sailing culture; suits travelers wanting an island escape without flying.

water.note: Municipal water is treated, but visitors commonly stick to bottled water as a precaution.

transit.pay: Minivan and bus fares are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in Eastern Caribbean dollars; there is no fare card system. Ferry tickets to Bequia and other Grenadine islands are bought at the dock or booth before boarding.
transit.hours: Minivans run roughly 6am-9pm on main routes, with limited service after dark; no scheduled night buses.
transit.note: Vans display route destinations in the windshield and can be flagged down anywhere along the route.

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often already added to restaurant bills, in which case extra tipping is not expected.

landmarks: Fort Charlotte
This 1806 hilltop fortress overlooks Kingstown harbour with cannons still aimed at the sea, offering the city's most sweeping panoramic photo opportunity.
St. George's Anglican Cathedral
A gleaming white colonial-era cathedral dating to 1820, prized for its elegant Georgian architecture and stained glass in the heart of downtown Kingstown.
Kingstown Botanic Gardens
Established in 1765, this is the oldest botanical garden in the Western Hemisphere, famous for rare breadfruit trees and the endangered St. Vincent parrot.
Cathedral of the Assumption
This eclectic Catholic cathedral blends Romanesque, Gothic, and Moorish styles into a whimsical, photogenic silhouette unlike any other church in the Caribbean.
La Soufrière Volcano
An active stratovolcano and the island's highest point, drawing hikers to its crater rim for dramatic views following its notable 2021 eruption.
Wallilabou Bay
A dramatic volcanic bay made famous as the filming location for Pirates of the Caribbean, with weathered wooden film-set structures still standing on the shore.
Bequia Island
A short ferry ride from Kingstown, this idyllic Grenadine island charms visitors with turquoise Admiralty Bay, colorful boats, and laid-back sailing culture.
Kingstown Harbour
The bustling waterfront where cruise ships, ferries, and fishing boats converge against a backdrop of green hills, capturing the city's maritime spirit.
Kingstown Public Market
A vibrant, chaotic market where vendors pile fresh tropical produce and fish under colorful awnings, offering an authentic slice of Vincentian daily life.
Young Island
A private resort islet just off Kingstown's coast, its lush thatched cottages and turquoise channel make it one of the most photographed views in St. Vincent.

train.note: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has no railway. Travel is by minibus, taxi and inter-island ferry.

bus.note: No international bus routes exist from this island nation. On St. Vincent, colourful shared minibuses run from the Kingstown terminal to towns around the island.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled international passenger ferry from Kingstown at present. Ferries are domestic within the Grenadines: Bequia Express and Admiralty Transport run frequently between Kingstown and Bequia, and Jaden Sun (https://jadensunferry.com/) continues south to Canouan, Mayreau and Union Island.
